figures.caption: Figure 1: A motivating example illustrating the entanglement of syntax and semantics in execution-based reward. Target C++ I is syntactically valid but semantically flawed; however, it exploits sparse test cases (where A[0] happens to be the minimum) to achieve a false positive pass (reward hacking). Conversely, Target C++ II maintains semantic equivalence (using min element) but receives a zero reward due to a compilation error.
